case.case_title: Jayasinghe v. Sub Inspector of Police, Jayakody and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1998) 2 Sri LR. 204

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained lawfully and brought before a judge in accordance with Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained illegally from 22.12.1996 to 26.12.1996 without being produced before a Magistrate.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents claimed the petitioner was arrested on 25.12.1996 and produced before the Magistrate on 26.12.1996, thus complying with the law.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained in police custody from 22.12.1996 to 26.12.1996 according to petitioner and witnesses.
Petitioner was produced before the Magistrate only on 26.12.1996.
Respondents claimed arrest on 25.12.1996 and production on 26.12.1996.
Petitioner was subjected to torture and ill-treatment during detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained be brought before a judge promptly and not held without legal authority. The court found the petitioner was held illegally for several days before being produced before a Magistrate, violating this constitutional right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court accepted the petitioner’s evidence and that of witnesses that he was detained from 22.12.1996 and only produced before a Magistrate on 26.12.1996. The respondents’ claim of arrest on 25.12.1996 was rejected. Thus, the detention was illegal under Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention without prompt production before a judicial authority is unlawful.
Delay in production before a judge violates constitutional protections.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner was illegally detained from 22.12.1996 to 26.12.1996 without being brought before a judge, violating Article 13(2).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation awarded to petitioner from respondents and the state.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was illegal because he was not brought before a judge promptly, directly violating the constitutional safeguard.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Petitioner was detained from 22.12.1996 and produced before the Magistrate only on 26.12.1996; respondents’ claim of arrest on 25.12.1996 was rejected.
